correctness.rationale: The round-three-sphere model of SU(2) makes the convolution radial. Conditional circular-arc overlap proves the cap-intersection function decreases with center separation, so layer-cake preserves radial monotonicity under convolution. Central antipodal oddness of the centered hemisphere density gives f_t(q)+f_t(-q)=2 and makes the hemisphere a TV-optimal event for every t. SU(2) characters and normalized angular Haar measure give explicit odd highest-weight multipliers and zero positive-even multipliers. Integrating the character expansion over the maximizing hemisphere gives the absolutely convergent TV series for all t>=1. Two-hemisphere intersection gives f_2=2(1-theta/pi), and direct angular integration yields 1/4-1/pi^2; the leading character proves the sharp mixing constant. A standalone finite checker passed the analytic multipliers and numerical consistency checks. No claim is inferred from finite data.

value.rationale: This is a fully specified nonabelian compact-group random walk for which all finite-time TV distances, a time-independent optimal distinguishing set, the complete two-step law, and the sharp asymptotic prefactor are determined. The key L1 conclusion is not a routine consequence of the known L2 multiplier list, and the natural problem of exact TV mixing is relevant to quantitative compact-group random walks. The result does not rely on artificial finite cutoffs or isolated numerical experiments.
